correctness.rationale: Exact two-step coordinate equations reduce, without assuming global semiconjugacy, to scalar cubic U↔V with g_t(w)=tw+w^3 (t=b(1-c), κ=abc>0). For U≠V, difference imposes t+U²+UV+V²+1=0; sum either U+V=0 giving exactly one symmetric orbit for t<-1, or UV=-1, U²+V²=-t giving precisely two additional sign-distinct orbits only t<-2. For symmetric pair, D conjugates opposite y-sign Jacobians and return derivative=(DJ)^2, characteristic λ³−λ²+2s, 2s=r²(r+1); remaining quadratic roots have modulus squared=r(r+1), so sink exactly 0<s<(√5−1)/4, saddle with two unstable for s*<s<1 and repeller s>1, excluding nonhyperbolic boundaries. For asymmetric UV=-1, exact return determinant 4 precludes sinks. Fresh independent SymPy computation checked derivative identities and determinant. Boundary t=-1,-2 counts and nonhyperbolic limits respected; no global attractor or nonlinear bifurcation claimed.
